identity.title: Ringed Substructure and a Gap at 1 au in the Nearest Protoplanetary Disk

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present long-baseline Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations of the 870 $\mu$m continuum emission from the nearest gas-rich protoplanetary disk, around TW Hya

evidence.quote: First, it is the closest gas-rich disk to Earth (cite: vanleeuwen07)

distance_source.value: van Leeuwen 2007 cited for closeness only

evidence.quote: First, it is the closest gas-rich disk to Earth (cite: vanleeuwen07)

question.value: Does the TW Hya disk show ringed substructure in 870 um continuum at ~1 AU resolution, and what could cause it?

evidence.quote: In this Letter, we present and analyze observations that shed new light on the substructure in the TW Hya disk.
The correlator processed four spectral windows centered at 344.5, 345.8, 355.1, and 357.1 GHz with bandwidths of 1875, 469, 1875, and 1875 MHz, respectively.
The array included 36, 31, and 34 antennas, respectively
configured to span baseline lengths from 20 m to 14 km
to provide a $24\times18$ mas synthesized beam (at P.A.=78$^\circ$)
have RMS noise levels around 35 $\mu$Jy beam$^{-1}$
The total on-target integration time was $\sim$2 hours.
The combined on-target integration time was 95 minutes.

findings_qualitative.value: Concentric rings with dark annuli at 1, 22, 37, 43 AU (tentative 12, 28, 31 AU); no significant non-axisymmetric structure

evidence.quote: The outer disk shows dark annuli at 22, 37, and 43 AU separated by more extended bright zones.

claims.hypothesis: Does TW Hya show ringed substructure at AU scales?
claims.experiment: 870 um long-baseline ALMA imaging combined with archival data
claims.result: Bright rings and narrow dark annuli at 1-43 AU with 5-30% contrasts
claims.finding: Ordered substructure on ~AU scales exists in the disk

evidence.quote: These data reveal a series of concentric ring-shaped substructures in the form of bright zones and narrow dark annuli (1–6 AU) with modest contrasts (5–30%).

claims.experiment: Compare radial profiles over polar angle ranges

evidence.quote: there are no statistically significant azimuthal variations in the observed emission

claims.experiment: Compare features with temperatures from a representative RADMC-3D model and literature mechanisms
claims.result: Outer features consistent with zonal flows; some near CO/N2 condensation fronts; 1 AU gap could be planet

evidence.quote: Other features, particularly a narrow dark annulus located only 1 AU from the star, could indicate interactions between the disk and young planets.

why_this_method.value: Two images chosen after experimentation to balance resolution and sidelobes

evidence.quote: After some experimentation, we settled on an analysis of two images made from the same composite dataset.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: H2O snowline as cause of 1-3 AU substructure judged unlikely

evidence.quote: we do not see a good reason to expect that the H$_2$O snowline itself would result in the substantial density depletion

limitations_admitted.value: Depth of the 1 AU annulus is uncertain because it is unresolved; model is not optimized and fails to match the profile

evidence.quote: Because it is unresolved, the depth of the dark annulus is difficult to determine unambiguously

referee_caveats_inferred: Temperature model is crude, so snowline associations are weak
Ring/gap radii and depths lack stated uncertainties
Dirty-beam sidelobes (~20%) could affect features in the robust 0 image
